<h>Lectio 1</h>
De libro Apocalýpsis beáti Ioánnis Apóstoli
<r>Apo 3:7-9</r>
<n>7</n> Et Ángelo Philadelphíæ Ecclésiæ scribe: Hæc dicit Sanctus et Verus, qui habet clavem David: qui áperit, et nemo claudit: claudit, et nemo áperit:
<n>8</n> Scio ópera tua. Ecce dedi coram te óstium apértum, quod nemo potest cláudere: quia módicam habes virtútem, et servásti verbum meum, et non negásti nomen meum.
<n>9</n> Ecce dabo de synagóga Sátanæ, qui dicunt se Iudǽos esse, et non sunt, sed mentiúntur.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Dignus es, Dómine, accípere librum, et aperíre signácula eius, allelúia: quóniam occísus es, et redemísti nos Deo

<r>℟.</r> In sánguine tuo, allelúia.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<r>Apo 3:9-12</r>
<n>9</n> Ecce fáciam illos ut véniant, et adórent ante pedes tuos: et scient quia ego diléxi te.
<n>10</n> Quóniam servásti verbum patiéntiæ meæ, et ego servábo te ab hora tentatiónis, quæ ventúra est in orbem univérsum tentáre habitántes in terra.
<n>11</n> Ecce vénio cito: tene quod habes, ut nemo accípiat corónam tuam.
<n>12</n> Qui vícerit, fáciam illum colúmnam in templo Dei mei, et foras non egrediétur ámplius: et scribam super eum nomen Dei mei, et nomen civitátis Dei mei novæ Ierúsalem, quæ descéndit de cælo a Deo meo, et nomen meum novum.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Ego sicut vitis fructificávi suavitátem odóris, allelúia:
* Transíte ad me, omnes qui concupíscitis me, et a generatiónibus meis adimplémini, allelúia, allelúia.
<r>℣.</r> Ego diligéntes me díligo; et qui mane vigiláverint ad me, invénient me.
<r>℟.</r> Transíte ad me, omnes qui concupíscitis me, et a generatiónibus meis adimplémini, allelúia, allelúia.

<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>Q</c>uinto Idus Aprílis Luna tértia. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>I</h>n Iudǽa sanctæ Maríæ Cléophæ, quam beátus Ioánnes Evangelísta sorórem sanctíssimæ Dei Genitrícis Maríæ núncupat, et cum hac simul iuxta crucem Iesu stetísse narrat.
<h>A</h>ntiochíæ sancti Próchori, qui fuit unus de septem primis Diáconis; et, fide ac miráculis clarus, martýrio coronátus est.
<h>R</h>omæ natális sanctórum Mártyrum Demétrii, Concéssi, Hilárii et Sociórum.
<h>C</h>æsaréæ, in Cappadócia, sancti Eupsýchii Mártyris, qui ob evérsum Fortúnæ fanum, sub Iuliáno Apóstata, martýrium consummávit.
<h>I</h>n Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Massylitanórum, in quorum die natáli sanctus Augustínus tractátum hábuit.
<h>S</h>írmii pássio sanctárum septem Vírginum et Mártyrum, quæ, dato simul prétio sánguinis, vitam mercátæ sunt ætérnam.
<h>A</h>midæ, in Mesopotámia, sancti Acátii Epíscopi, qui pro rediméndis captívis étiam vasa Ecclésiæ conflávit ac véndidit.
<h>R</h>otómagi sancti Hugónis, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>I</h>n civitáte Diénsi, in Gállia, sancti Marcélli Epíscopi, miráculis clari.
<h>M</h>óntibus, in Hannónia, beátæ Waldetrúdis, vitæ sanctimónia et miráculis claræ.
<h>R</h>omæ Translátio córporis sanctæ Mónicæ, matris beáti Augustíni Epíscopi; quod, ex Ostiis Tiberínis, Martíno Quinto Summo Pontífice, in Urbem delátum, in Ecclésia eiúsdem beáti Augustíni honorífice recónditum fuit.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.a27bbfd726:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>A</c>pril 9th 2027, the 3rd day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>I</h>n Judea, holy Mary of Cleophas, sister of Mary the most Holy Mother of God.
<h>A</h>t Antioch, holy Prochorus, one of the seven first deacons. He was illustrious for his faith and miracles, and was crowned with martyrdom. [He was the 3rd of the seven deacons, and 66th of the 72 disciples. He was a nephew of St Stephen. After being with St John in Asia, he was made Bishop of Nicomedia, in Bithynia, by St Peter, and later on sent to Antioch.]
<h>A</h>t Rome, the holy martyrs Demetrius, Concessus, Hilary, and their Companions.
<h>A</h>t Caesarea, in Cappadocia, [in the year 362,] the holy martyr Eupsychius, who was crowned with martyrdom under the Emperor Julian the Apostate for casting down the shrine of Fortune.
<h>I</h>n Africa, the holy martyrs of Massylita, [probably Fez,] upon whose birthday holy Augustine made a discourse.
<h>A</h>t Sirmium, suffered seven holy Virgins, all martyrs, who purchased eternal life at the price of their blood.
<h>A</h>t Diarbekr, in Mesopotamia, [in the fifth century,] holy Acatius, Bishop of that see, who even melted down and sold the vessels of the Church to redeem captives withal.
<h>A</h>t Rouen, the holy Confessor Hugh, Bishop of that see, [in the year 730.]
<h>I</h>n the city of Die, [in the sixth century,] holy Marcellus, Bishop thereof, who was famous for miracles.
<h>A</h>t Mons, in Hainaut, [in the year 686,] the blessed Waldetrude, [First Abbess of Mons and Foundress of that City,] famous for the holiness of her life and for her miracles.
<h>A</h>t Rome is commemorated the translation of the body of holy Monica, mother of the blessed Augustine, Bishop [of Hippo,] which the supreme Pontiff Martin V caused to be brought into the city from Ostia, and honourably buried in the church of the said blessed Augustine, [in the year 1439.]
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
